purpose: Three render protocols with a RenderSpec fingerprint each. A metric is only comparable across runs when every fingerprint field matches; a field marked 'unpropagated' is one the current tools do not carry from training to evaluation (or from evaluation to the record), so two reports can differ on it without either report saying so.

code_anchors.backend_render: cloudstudio_3dgs/training/backend.py :: GsplatBackend.render (lines ~441-556): builds the gsplat rasterization() call; camera_model from sample.camera_model, with_ut/with_eval3d = (fisheye or pinhole_with_ut), rasterize_mode = 'classic' for fisheye else self.pinhole_rasterize_mode, global_z_order = not fisheye, render_mode RGB / RGB+ED (pinhole z-depth) / RGB-Ed (UT euclidean range), composite rgb + (1-alpha)*background when background_rgb is given
code_anchors.load_backend: tools/sharpness_metrics.py :: _load_backend (line 148): GsplatBackend(device, cap_max, gsplat_lock, mcmc noise 0); backend.color_model = config.color_model; backend.sh_degree = config.sh_degree unless the caller passes the model's degree. It does NOT set pinhole_rasterize_mode or pinhole_with_ut from the config, so eval renders use the GsplatBackend defaults ('classic', False) regardless of what the training config says.

A_face4_pinhole_classic.role: training camera; the number every existing battery/sharpness/three-way report is computed in
A_face4_pinhole_classic.target: Face4 face PNG from the face cache (a resampling of the fisheye photo), compared inside the renderer mask

intrinsics_K.value: K_face per (camera, face) from <face cache>/face_manifest.json cameras[*].faces[*].K_face; house0305 v8/v9: yaw faces fx=fy=1039.691749 cx=728 cy=1456 (1456x2912), pitch faces fx=fy=2308.921016 cx=1456 cy=728 (2912x1456); minus tile crop (x,y) when tile_views are given

distortion.value: none (radial_coeffs zeros; not passed to gsplat for pinhole)
distortion.source: backend.py render: radial = None if pinhole

pixel_centre_convention.value: face cache declares pixel_convention='pixel_center_plus_half' (face_manifest.json); gsplat rasterization samples pixel centres at +0.5 with K in pixel units
pixel_centre_convention.source: face manifest field; NOT carried on the sample or in any report

resolution.value: face native size at factor 1 (1456x2912 / 2912x1456); Tile crops = view crop size (e.g. 2157x1456 for a pitch face crop)

sh_degree.value: model degree (sqrt(K0+KN)-1), forced by the three eval tools; eval configs delivery_eval*.json still say sh_degree=0 and sharpness_metrics.py main() does NOT override (renders DC-only for an SH1 checkpoint)
sh_degree.status: partially propagated: reports carry gaussian_count and step but not the degree actually rendered (roundtrip report is the exception: it records sh_degree)

colour_space.value: 8-bit sRGB PNG / 255 compared directly against SH-evaluated RGB clamped to [0,1]; no linearisation or gamma anywhere in the chain (implicit sRGB-as-linear)
colour_space.source: evaluate_probe_views target = image/255; backend returns raw rasterization rgb

exposure_policy.value: training learns a per-exposure gain (exposure_compensation.enabled=true, lr 0.005 in delivery_eval.json); NONE of evaluate_probe_views / build_three_way_compare / roundtrip / sharpness_metrics applies it at eval; the tile merge applies one exposure_gain_applied per tile (merge_report.json: 0.899/0.943/0.938/0.963 for G9) so merged.pt colours already carry a per-tile global gain
exposure_policy.source: trainer.py ExposureCompensationConfig; tools grep shows no 'exposure' in the eval tools

background.value: ViewBackgroundLibrary per-view sky-dome backdrop (view_backgrounds_*/manifest, downsample 4, background_rgb white) when the config has background_image_manifest; otherwise constant white (1,1,1); roundtrip control uses black vs white
background.status: propagated only as the manifest path in the config; reports record background_rgb (three-way) or nothing (battery)

rasterize_mode.value: 'classic' (GsplatBackend default; pinhole_rasterize_mode from the config is NOT applied by _load_backend, so an 'antialiased'-trained checkpoint would be evaluated classic)

with_ut.value: false (pinhole_with_ut default False; _load_backend does not read the config's pinhole_with_ut)

clipping_near_far.value: gsplat defaults (near_plane 0.01, far_plane 1e10): render() passes neither

alpha_rule.value: rgb = rendered + (1-alpha)*background; alpha returned un-composited; PSNR over rgb_mask pixels; foreground alpha p05 over mask; global_z_order=True

coordinate_frame.value: s1_local (dataset_manifest.coordinate_frame), pose_convention c2w_opencv; face c2w = c2w_base @ [R_face|0]; tile checkpoints use identity coordinate transform (s1_local_identity_v1)
coordinate_frame.source: dataset manifest; face_dataset.py; tile run coordinate_transform_manifest.json

view_set.value: evaluate_probe_views default: face4_val cache of the CONFIG's dataset version with stride len//48 (delivery_eval.json -> house0305_sop_v8/face4_val, 360 faces, stride 7, indexes 0,7,...,329); --tile-views: the Tile's own cropped training views
view_set.status: propagated as view_set label only ('held_out_faces'), not as the split the checkpoint trained on

pixel_mask.value: renderer mask = warped source mask AND fov valid AND face weight > 0.02 (face manifest mask_semantics); person masks folded in upstream; --tile-owned additionally removes foreign-tile pixels

B_original_fisheye_ut.role: the photo the customer took, rendered through the KB4 fisheye with 3DGUT; the only protocol whose target is the untouched original JPEG
B_original_fisheye_ut.target: original 2912x2912 fisheye JPEG (recording camera/<side>/<timestamp>.jpg) inside the mask manifest's valid circle and person mask

intrinsics_K.value: dataset_manifest cameras[*].intrinsic / factor: left fl 787.6402706 cx 1454.3167 cy 1452.1973 (right differs by <0.3 px / 3.1 px cy); calibration_source accepted_independent_pos_prior_at

distortion.value: OPENCV_FISHEYE k1 0.07691 k2 -0.00680 k3 -0.00538 k4 0.00036 (left); passed as radial_coeffs

pixel_centre_convention.value: K in pixel units; gsplat UT projection convention; no field on the sample

sh_degree.value: sharpness_metrics.py main() uses config.sh_degree (0 in delivery_eval*.json) -> DC-only for SH1 models unless the config is edited; no model-degree override in that entry point

colour_space.value: JPEG sRGB/255 vs raw SH RGB, no linearisation

exposure_policy.value: no per-exposure gain applied at eval (same as A)

background.value: config.background_color constant (white in delivery_eval.json); no sky-dome library on this path; --exclude-sky restricts the mask to LiDAR depth support instead

with_eval3d.value: true (forced for fisheye); range semantics euclidean_ray_range_m

view_set.value: S1TrainingDataset split='val' of the CONFIG's split manifest (delivery_eval.json -> v8 val = 90 images; delivery_eval_v9.json -> v9 val = 2 images) with --views indexes (default 0 40 80)

pixel_mask.value: mask manifest (fisheye valid circle x person mask) [x depth support with --exclude-sky]

B_original_fisheye_ut.not_yet_run_here: no report in C:/Peter/3dgs-runs/house0305_sop uses this protocol against a merged delivery; all G9/C1/R1 numbers are protocol A

C_final_ply_external_viewer.role: what the customer sees: the exported PLY in a viewer we do not control (SuperSplat / Potree-GS / vendor viewer)
C_final_ply_external_viewer.target: human inspection and, where possible, viewer screenshots at poses exported from protocol A/B (no ground-truth photo inside the viewer)

camera_model.value: viewer pinhole; viewer-defined FOV; no fisheye

intrinsics_K.value: not transferable; only the c2w pose and a vertical FOV can be set

sh_degree.value: what the PLY carries: export_gaussian_ply writes f_dc + f_rest (G9 export: 3 SH rest coeffs = degree 1); viewers may cap (SuperSplat renders up to degree 3, some viewers DC-only)
sh_degree.source: tools/export_gaussian_ply.py SH_C0 = 0.28209479; delivery_g9/deliver_status.txt '3 SH rest coeffs'
sh_degree.status: PLY carries it; viewer behaviour unpropagated

colour_space.value: viewers apply their own tone/gamma (SuperSplat renders in linear then sRGB-encodes; others treat SH RGB as sRGB)
colour_space.status: unpropagated; must be pinned per viewer before any cross-protocol colour comparison

exposure_policy.value: PLY carries merged per-tile gains baked into colours; no per-view gain exists in the viewer

background.value: viewer background colour; no sky dome

rasterize_mode.value: viewer's own splatting (typically classic EWA in WebGL); no antialiased/Mip compensation

alpha_rule.value: viewer compositing; opacity threshold at export (export_checkpoint_ply min_opacity; G9 export kept 13.58M of 19.31M, i.e. an export-time opacity cull)
alpha_rule.status: export threshold propagated in deliver_status only

coordinate_frame.value: s1_local unless align_gaussian_ply / a reference alignment transform was applied; reference USAgs.ply lives in its own frame and is aligned by a rigid transform with a recorded median NN residual

view_set.value: free navigation; for evidence use the ROI registry parent images' poses

C_final_ply_external_viewer.roundtrip_gate: tools/roundtrip_checkpoint_ply.py proves checkpoint -> PLY -> checkpoint tensor equality (1e-6) and same-backend render equality, with controls; it does not prove the viewer renders the PLY the way protocol A does

cross_protocol_rules: Never compare a protocol A number with a protocol B number; the target images differ (resampled face vs original JPEG), the projection differs, and the masks differ.

A report must state the view set AND the split the checkpoint trained on; 'held_out_faces' from evaluate_probe_views only names the cache it read, not hold-out status (see 01_view_membership_summary.json: 48/48 battery views are in v9 train).
Before any SH-sensitive comparison, record the rendered degree; delivery_eval*.json declare 0.
Exposure: G9 merged colours carry per-tile gains; a single-tile checkpoint does not; three-way strips of a tile vs the merge are not colour-comparable without the gain.
